svg.title: macOS · Photo viewer / grading editor · Text tab · 1000×700
svg.desc: Mirrors App/PhotoViewerView.swift (textTab) hosting App/Overlay/OverlayEditingPanel.swift — the Text page of the editor rail, rebuilt 2026-08-31 from the Claude Design "Text Features" spec (multiple layers, type fundamentals, bounding boxes, a Masks tab). Window, media column and timeline strip are photo-viewer.svg's (same staged project, same moment); only the rail differs. THE PAGE edits a LIST of text layers stored in the per-project overlays.json sidecar (OverlayDocument: overlays + customMasks + mask dials; persisted on finished gestures plus a 2s safety net, exit and window close; a second window on the same project can never bulldoze the sidecar because persists no-op when unchanged; every field past the spike's original five decodes with decodeIfPresent, so a sidecar written before the schema grew keeps its text instead of reading as empty). ORDER IS STACKING ORDER: row 1 is the frontmost layer, and the compositor walks the array in reverse so row 1 paints last. Drag a card by its grip to reorder. LAYER ROW: grip · visibility eye · title (the text itself, newlines shown as ↵) · an animation indicator (accent when the layer has a reveal) · onion skin · expand chevron. Hidden layers are skipped in the preview AND the export. Onion skin draws a layer at full strength ignoring its animation — editor-only scaffolding, never baked — and is disabled without an animation, because with no reveal the text is always drawn; a hidden layer with onion on ghosts at 34%. EXPANDED, four disclosures (a card opens with TEXT & SIZE showing): TEXT & SIZE — the string (multi-line; Return inserts a newline, so on iOS the keyboard toolbar's Done is the exit), Mode Free · Box, and Size as a fraction of the frame's LONG edge with the readout in px of the DELIVERED file (the preview is capped at 2000px / 1100px mid-scrub, so quoting against it would change as you scrub). Then Angle (2026-09-02): the layer's own rotation about its anchor, the SAME RotationSlider the Edit tab levels the whole picture with (±10°, centre-snapped, degrees readout, double-click the label to zero) in its inline shape. Layers live in the LEVELLED frame's space: when the project's rotation moves, every existing layer is re-expressed to stay pinned to the scene — anchor remapped, angle carried, size and box grown by the crop-in — so a layer that was already on the project tilts with the picture and its Angle reads the project's angle; a layer added afterwards starts at 0° and reads level. The rasterizer turns the whole block (lines, slide offsets, underlines) about the anchor with one CTM rotation; the preview proxy, the outline and the eight box handles turn with it, and a handle drag is read along the box's own axes. Auto-size in box mode dims this slider and turns the readout amber. TYPE — family (SF Pro · Helvetica Neue · Georgia · Avenir Next · Futura · Courier New; an absent family falls back to the system face at raster time), B/I/U, alignment, five swatches (White · Ink · Accent · Amber · Sky), and More… — a popover holding Kerning (a fraction of the em, so it scales with the type), Line height, Paragraph, and Auto-Size font with Min/Max, all three box-only. Auto-size solves BOTH axes by bisection against a FIXED reference long edge, so the chosen step is a property of the layer and cannot differ between a 1100px scrub and a 2000px settled render. INTELLIGENT PLACEMENT — None, then the project's regions (Sky · Land, or a custom mask's names), then Custom, which is a route to the Masks tab rather than a value. ANIMATION — None · Fade · Slide, a From direction for Slide, and Set Start / Set End pinning the band to the playhead (the playhead is the precision instrument, so there are no draggable band handles); reveals are per-character with overlap 0.6, eased by the house cubic, and the settled raster is byte-identical to no animation — the resting layout IS the end state. REMOVE TEXT — red, per layer. ON THE PREVIEW (this tab only): every visible layer is draggable — baked at rest, a SwiftUI proxy takes over during the drag (frozen committed centre + translation ÷ drawn size, unit-clamped, committed and persisted on release; a cancelled drag heals back), and dragging a layer selects it. A centre snap within 0.018 pins the axis and draws an amber guide (desc-only). The SELECTED layer gets chrome: a solid accent outline for FREE, a dashed amber box with eight resize handles for BOX (each handle moves its own edge and leaves the opposite one put), a mode+text badge, and — with auto-size on — an AUTO chip reading the resolved px and where it sits in the Min…Max bracket. STAGED HERE: 4 layers. Row 1 "LetsLapse" is selected, FREE, Sky-placed, with a fade whose reveal has not started at this playhead (so the composite draws nothing and only the chrome marks the spot). Row 2 is BOX + auto-size + onion skin, Georgia italic, Land-placed. Row 3 is hidden. Row 4 is Courier with wide tracking. Exports bake exactly this page's state — same compositing core, same masks, dials from the sidecar; hidden layers and onion skin are the two things the export deliberately does not carry. Hooks: LL_EDITOR=<uuid|latest>, LL_RAIL=text, LL_SEG_MODEL=<path>. Verified against the running Mac app 2026-08-31; Angle row verified 2026-09-02 (project "Day to night 5k dng i16" levelled +4.9°: the pre-existing box layer read +4.9°, a freshly added layer read 0°).

g.text: Drag the text on the preview to place it. Where it rests
is where every animation ends. Drag a layer by its grip
to reorder — the top layer sits in front.
